source.title: Native Geometry vs. Linear Recoverability: How Alignment Changes Platonic Scaling
source.authors: Angus Hoy; Austin Lutterbach; Jasper Chong; A. Kumar; Michael J. Smith

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices A–I.
record.tranche_reason: Tests scale-related representation correspondence using native cosine neighbourhood overlap and supervised Ridge alignment, a conceptual comparison of convergence that distinguishes native geometry from linear recoverability.
record.gate_note: The paper tests Legacy→HSC correspondence on matched astronomy objects, with additional same-dataset cross-model and unpaired controls. It does not test vision-language image-caption alignment, same-architecture seed convergence, or recurrence of individual interpretable features. Reported prior-work results are not included as rows. Values used only to choose settings are omitted.
record.test_reason: The paper argues that apparent PRH convergence depends on the comparison method: native cosine mKNN versus supervised Ridge recoverability. It reports numbers for both. Most results compare one model's embeddings of two surveys (Legacy vs HSC) of the same objects, not different models. The genuinely cross-model evidence is the same-dataset control in Appendix F (101 cross-family pairs).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Scale strengthens supervised linear recoverability more clearly than native cosine-neighbourhood correspondence, which rises only weakly. This does not establish convergence to a shared native metric geometry: the maps are anisotropic and absolute mKNN is low. The main comparisons are between each model's Legacy and HSC embeddings of the same objects, not between different models. The authors frame the result as convergence depending on the transformation class.
record.recipe_differences: Uses matched astronomy-survey embeddings and mutual k-nearest-neighbour overlap, with a supervised affine/Ridge map as a comparison to native cosine geometry. This is not a direct reproduction of the cited PRH or convergent-learning methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Correspondence and slope depend on native versus Ridge-aligned comparison and on mapping direction. Forward amplification remains positive over k ∈ {5, 10, 25, 50} and Ridge α ∈ {0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100}; family-level positivity varies with k and direction. Independent PCA rank and SAE inference-time TopK are also varied.

fits_no_version.finding: For the same model embedding two surveys of the same objects, Ridge recoverability grows with model size faster than native cosine correspondence. This holds in 5/5 families and at fixed PCA256 dimension.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within-model cross-sensor (multi-view) correspondence of the same objects increases with model scale under linear recoverability.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-survey Ridge maps are strongly anisotropic and far from scaled-orthogonal (Dsim ≈0.88–0.91). Yet about 5% of singular directions carry 90% of the mKNN lift.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Maps linking representations of different views are non-isometric, but their functionally relevant part is low-dimensional.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE/BSF features underperform dense embeddings under matched Ridge alignment. Their size trend is non-positive across TopK.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse dictionary features do not expose more cross-view shared structure than dense embeddings.

fits_no_version.finding: An unpaired nonlinear cross-survey map reaches above-chance relational mKNN (0.012–0.023), with non-monotonic size dependence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unpaired cross-view translation is weakly possible but not scale-monotonic.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2026 Workshop: Symmetry and Geometry in Neural Representations (NeurReps)
record.problems: The evidence covers five model families in one astronomy setting, uses one frozen split, and requires paired Ridge supervision for the main recoverability result. Native correspondence remains low. The paper itself notes that one global affine map may only weakly approximate the underlying relationship. No capability measure is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported result was omitted due to the 60-row limit. Some supplementary diagnostics not separately rowed include weak local structure in Ridge residuals, residual cosine similarity ≈0.01, patch-intercept held-out MSE reduction ≪0.1%, and pooled interaction θ=0.00451 (Appendices C and D).

untested.parts: No native cross-model size trend is reported. The cross-model scale evidence is only a descriptive Ridge-gain slope. There is no capability measure and no variation of modality or objective.
No vision-language or image-caption models are tested.
Stitching and relative representations are not tested. An unpaired map is tested only across surveys, not across models.
No recurrence of specific features or circuits across models. SAE/BSF features are used only as Ridge inputs.
There are no native slopes per k. Input distribution and out-of-distribution inputs are not varied.
No plateau analysis. There is no test of whether shared data or objectives cause the alignment.

missing.what: Cross-model scale trend: mutual Ridge gain βmin(Gsym)=+0.026 and directional asymmetry βmin(Adir)=+0.017 against the smaller model's log size. Also, larger→smaller gain ≈0.059 vs smaller→larger ≈0.062.
Excluding I-JEPA, forward T=0.00537 (4/4 families) and T256=0.00673.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked the cross-survey rows to V1/V4/V7. Those rows compare one model's embeddings of two surveys, not independently trained models, so they were relinked to V6 (method dependence) or moved to fits_no_version. Only Appendix F is cross-model. The reader's V7 'challenges' label was wrong: low, incomplete correspondence supports V7. The rows marked 'reversed' (r32/r34/r36) compare the study's own SAE and Dense variants, not a version.

versions.untested_parts: Tests scale and correspondence across five visual model families in one astronomy setting, not broad variation in modalities, objectives, or training data; parameter count is used as the scale measure, without a capability evaluation.
No paired image-caption vision-language models are tested.
No same-architecture models trained from different initializations are compared for shared features or subspaces.

Tests supervised affine/Ridge maps on paired training objects. Does not test stitching, relative representations, or mappings learned without paired data as a general method; an unpaired nonlinear control is reported but is not a test of all those approaches.
SAE and BSF feature representations are compared after Ridge alignment, but recurrence or identity of specific interpretable features or circuits across models is not measured.
Compares native cosine-neighbourhood correspondence with Ridge-aligned correspondence and varies k. Does not compare broad input distributions or out-of-distribution inputs.
Finds incomplete native correspondence and anisotropic maps, but does not establish a plateau or test whether shared training data/objectives cause alignment instead of a common model of reality.
